result.reportText:
# Rung W, walk infers a generic dotted method's own static arguments (`rung-walk-method-sargs`, climb batch 17)

- problem: ledger row 21, a generic method's own static arguments are not inferred under walk (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:99`); F-248, rung L's generic `distribute` stops a nested reduction under walk without this fix (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:166`); the probe's base runs, `explorations/perf-probes/walk-generic-static/REPORT.md:13-30`.
- spec: `Specification/basic/inference.tex:47-75` ("The Static Arguments of a Call": a declaration is chosen on the parameter types it declares, then instantiated from the arguments); `Specification/basic/expressions/method-invocation.tex:49-52` ("most method invocations do not include them; the static arguments are statically inferred").
- precedent: the function path's call of a generic declaration, `GenericFunctionOrConstructor.applyInnerPossiblyGeneric` through `EvaluatorBase.inferAndInstantiateGenericFunction` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/GenericFunctionOrConstructor.java:51-57`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/EvaluatorBase.java:72-78`); the declared-domain comparison of an own generic, `moreSpecificDeclaration`, `declaredBelow` and `instanceHolding` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:2138-2145`, `:2117-2128`, `:2094-2110` at 3aea3da53); the probe's commit fd7056abf.
- deviation: part A keeps no per-argument-type cache, where `GenericFunctionOrConstructor.applyInnerPossiblyGeneric` keeps one (`GenericFunctionOrConstructor.java:52-56`); the comparison of a generic dotted method on its declared domain is a helper of its own (`OverloadedFunction.java:2035-2086`), not a widening of `ownGeneric`, `declaredBelow` or `instanceHolding`, which walk's load check shares (`OverloadedFunction.java:2051`, `:2117` at 3aea3da53); the specification's text names the new rows NEW-W-1 to NEW-W-3 by placeholder (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:288`, `:291`, `:418`; `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2120-2124`).
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/DottedMethodApplication.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java`, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`.

## 1. What changed and why

Under walk an object holds a generic method as its symbolic instance, at static arguments that stand for themselves. A dotted call that wrote no static argument applied that symbolic instance as it was (`DottedMethodApplication.java:166`, the team's line `return cl.applyMethod(self, args);`, the same at a874948ac:166). So the call failed with "Unification error" or "Symbolic type T is being matched to value". An overloaded method set took the symbolic instance for a plain method, so a call that only the generic method fits found "no matching overload". The specification infers the static arguments of every call that does not write them, method invocations included (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:47-75`; `Specification/basic/expressions/method-invocation.tex:49-52`), and walk already does so for functions (P-45, F-26).

The change is in walk only (`git diff --stat 3aea3da53 -- ProjectFortress/src`: two files, +100 -10):

- **Part A, the probe's code as it is** (`DottedMethodApplication.java:166-187`). `applyInnerPossiblyGeneric` applies `instanceFor(cl, args)`. For a symbolic instance of a generic method, that is the instance `EvaluatorBase.inferAndInstantiateGenericFunction` infers from the arguments in the generic method's evaluation environment (`GenericMethod.evaluationEnv`). It does not use the trait method's member environment, which is empty. `isSymbolicInstance` recognizes such an instance: a `MethodInstance` and a `FunctionClosure` whose instance arguments are symbolic.
- **Part B, the probe's code as it is** (`OverloadedFunction.java:1911-1914`, `:1981-1984`, `:2002`, `:2008`, `:2018-2033`). `bestMatchWithCoercion` and `bestMatchInternal` treat a symbolic instance as its generic method when they choose and instantiate an overload. They go through `genericOf` and `inferenceEnv`, which return what the code used before for a real generic function (`gsfn` and `gsfn.getWithin()`).
- **Part B, beyond the probe** (`OverloadedFunction.java:1999`, `:2035-2086`). With the probe's code, a generic dotted method's instance was compared with the set's other methods on its inferred domain, and that domain can tie a plain method's. `Describer.describe(Circle)`, for an inherited `describe[\T extends Shape\](x: T)` beside the object's own `describe(x: Circle)`, answered `"generic"` where the base answered `"circle"` (section 5, `MInstCompare`). `bestMatchInternal` now calls `preferredDeclaration`: when one of the two is such a symbolic instance and exactly one of their declared domains lies inside the other, the inner one wins; otherwise `moreSpecificDeclaration` decides, as before. `methodDeclaredBelow` reads a symbolic instance's domain as its declared domain, each static parameter standing for itself. It decides whether some instance of the other generic method holds that domain, as `instanceHolding` does for an own generic, from values that carry only types, and memoizes the answer per pair.

Part B infers again on every call of an overloaded method, since `OverloadedMethod` keeps no cache (the probe's section 7). The pair comparison is memoized.

Not changed, each left as the brief leaves it: written static arguments on an overloaded receiver (row 744, `DottedMethodApplication.typeApply`, `:124-143`); an expected type that alone fixes the argument (row 510); a generic dotted method beside a plain one in one declaration list (NEW-W-1); `bool` static parameters (row 307, NEW-W-2).

## 3. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The checker reads a `where` clause in `KindEnv`: the territory map's "where clauses" row says "`staticenv/KindEnv.scala:126` ... type bindings handled in `TypeAnalyzer.extendJ`" (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:237`).

- `TypeAnalyzer.extend` reaches it through `env.extend(params, where)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:952`, `:955`).
- The overloading checker, the type checker and the thunker reach it through the same call.
- A call is checked against the declaration's arrow, which `makeArrowFromFunctional` builds.

These are the probe's two places, and the brief's.

The library's way, by kind:

- The generic over `K`: the team's own commented line (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3235` at 3aea3da53) and Emoto's comment (`Library/Generator2.fss:172`). Every pair in the library fits `K` as its lift type: `MaxSumReductionPair[\T\] extends ReductionPair[\T,Maybe[\T\]\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3402-3403`), and `ProdReduction`'s overload answers `PossibleReductionPair[\T\]` (`:3434`).
- The method condition: the team's form `where { T extends B }` on a declaration (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:350`). `MaxSumReductionPair`'s own bound `{ AdditiveGroup[\T\], StandardMax[\T\] }` (`:3402`) is what the condition supplies.
- The cast: the identities' eight other branches are each `cast[\T\](...)` (`:3365-3376`). No other numeral fallback stands in the two functions: 2 sites, both changed.
- `embiggen`:
  - The library writes a nullary big operator over a monoid as `BigReduction[\T,T\](R)`, answering `BigReduction[\T,T\]`, when its body and unwrap are the identity. `grep -n '^opr BIG [^(]*()' Library/*.fss` finds 20: `SUM`, `PROD`, `BIG AND`, `BIG OR`, `BIG BITXOR`, `BIG LEXICO`, `BIG SQCAP`, `BIG SQCUP`, `BIG MIN`, `BIG MAX`, `BIG MINNUM`, `BIG MAXNUM`, `List`'s and `PureList`'s `BIG CONCAT`, `Set`'s `BIG UNION` and `BIG INTERSECTION`, and `PrefixSet`'s three.
  - The library writes `Comprehension` where the body or the unwrap is not the identity: `BIG ||`, `BIG //`, `BIG MINMAX`, the tuple min-max operators and `BIG RELATION`.
  - The team's `BIG MINNUM` and `BIG MAXNUM` (`:3476-3478`, `:3483-3485`) are exactly `embiggen`'s body over `RR64`: `BigReduction[\RR64,RR64\](MapReduceReduction[\RR64\](fn ..., 0.0/0.0))`.
  - Two team callers already declare that type for `embiggen`'s result (`Library/Pairs.fss:75`, `:106`, `:112`; `ProjectFortress/tests/WordCountSmall.fss:74`, `:81`).
  - The team's note when it added `embiggen`, commit `183015086` (jmaessen, 2008-04-28): "it's impossible for us to provide a definition that actually works today and that will also pass static type checking; when the time comes it will be more expedient and smart to rip out the hacks and use the proper type information instead". `MIMapReduceReduction` is that hack: the `Any`-typed twin of the typed `MapReduceReduction`, which already existed (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3688`).

Where a precedent repaired the same defect:

- The identities' numeral fallback stands at 2 sites in its file, and both changed.
- `embiggen` is the one `Comprehension[\T,T,Any,Any\]` result in `FortressLibrary.fss`.
- Its 6 callers in three files are the only big operators in the library declared `Comprehension[\X,X,Any,Any\]`, outside the compiler's files (`grep -rn 'Any,Any\\\]' Library/*.fs?`).

## 4. What the specification settles

- A trait constraint bounds the variable it names inside the declaration (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:333-353`). So `x.show()` in a method whose condition says `T extends Shows` is well typed, and `MaxReduction[\T\]` is well formed in an overload whose condition says `T extends StandardMax[\T\]`.
- A call to a declaration with a constraint on its own static parameter applies only to arguments that meet it (the same section; `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, "The Static Arguments of a Call"). So `g("s")` is refused.
- The Return Type Rule is read over every instance of a generic declaration (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:555-560`, "Declarations with Static Parameters"). So only the generic over `K` passes beside `SumReduction`'s overloads (`explorations/perf-probes/generic-distribute/REPORT.md` section 3).
- The team's note "where clauses ... are not supported yet" (`Specification/basic/functions.tex:15-19`) stays true. The code generator refuses a declaration with a `where` clause (row 701), as `XXXWhereBoundChecker` now shows.
- The specification is silent on the identities' fallback for a non-number `T` (row 436, F-243), and on `embiggen`, a library helper with no entry.

# Climb batch 17, rung C: four checker rows (737, 738, 739, 681)

- problem: the batch 16 review's reading of row 737, "Repairing row 737 by matching parameter types takes `:130` out for good" (`explorations/reviews/batch-16-review.md:21`); rows 737, 738, 739 and 681 (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:278`, `:421`, `:422`, `:193`)
- spec: `Specification/basic/components/type-inference.tex:29` (row 737); `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:525-529` (row 739); `Specification/basic/inference.tex:57`, `:71` and `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:55` (row 681); row 738's message is not in the specification: `grep -rn 'Invalid overloading' Specification --include=*.tex` prints nothing
- precedent: the export check's matching of a component's declaration to an api's by `ExportChecker.equalTypes` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:431`, `:479`); rung K's per-provider set with its `implemented` filter (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:166-185`)
- deviation: the top-level set's `implemented` filter does not use the precedent's subtyping test of two instantiated trait types. The top level has no instance of the declaring traits' static parameters, so the filter instead looks for the implementing declaration's trait among the ancestors of its declaration (`OverloadingChecker.scala:141-160`); row 737's match takes no declaration where several api declarations fit a declaration that leaves out a parameter type (`ApiTypeExtractor.scala:77-83`)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ApiTypeExtractor.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/Formula.scala`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`

Branch `wip/rung-checker-four-rows`, from the base 3aea3da53. The code's last commit is 9697e3838. The tests and the specification edit are on the branch beside it. This report could not be written there: the harness refused the write.

## 1. What changed and why

**Row 737, an api declaration chosen by its parameter types.** `ApiTypeExtractor.isExported` gave a function that leaves out its return type the return type of the first api declaration of its name, in the identity-hash order of `DeclaredFunction`s, comparing no parameter types (`ApiTypeExtractor.scala:116-122` at the base). It now takes the one api declaration of the name whose parameter types are the function's own. The comparison is the one the export check makes between a component's declaration and the api's (`ExportChecker.equalTypes`), and a parameter the function leaves untyped matches any. Where none or several fit, it takes none, and the declaration keeps what it elides (`ApiTypeExtractor.scala:77-83`, `:121-126`, `:193-209`). "Type Inference for Components" expands each construct "corresponding to declarations in APIs exported by C" with the api's types (`type-inference.tex:29`); the declaration that corresponds is the one with the function's own parameter types. The method branch had the same first pick for a dotted method (`:91` at the base) and a functional method (`:98`). Those two other sites of the defect in the file are repaired by the same helper (`:97-108`). So `BIG LEXICO(g)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:129-130`) takes `TotalComparison` from `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:98`, and `:130` drops out of both stages.

**Row 738, the kind word.** The per-provider message tested the compilation unit for an object, which a unit never is. It now tests the trait or object (`OverloadingChecker.scala:370`): 'Invalid overloading of m in object O'.

**Row 739, the top-level set's abstract functional methods.** In a component the top-level set read only declarations with a body, functional methods among them (`OverloadingChecker.scala:118-121` at the base). So an abstract `h(self)` beside an unrelated top-level `h(x: String)` was never put to the Meet Rule for functions, which `overloading.tex:525-529` applies to a functional method beside a function. It now reads every functional method of the component, abstract ones too (`OverloadingChecker.scala:125-126`). Like rung K's per-provider set, it leaves out an abstract one that a declaration of a strict subtype with the same parameter types implements (`:135-160`). Two versions came before the final one, each corrected after a measurement:
- The first (68b58b237) read every abstract functional method with no filter. The distance stage then refused the one library's `QQ`: its only comprised object, `Ratio`, declares `QQ`'s abstract `numerator(self)` and `denominator(self)` with the same parameter type. The message was 'There are multiple declarations of numerator with the same parameter type: (QQ & {Ratio})' at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:593,671` and `:594,672` (first distance run, 'DISTANCE UP   49 -> 50 (+1)', `kind overloading 0 -> 2`). That is the shape the precedent's filter exists for.
- The second (b3d52f1de) added the filter with the precedent's test, the analyzer's subtyping of the two declaring traits' types. At the top level those types name static parameters that no kind environment holds. The distance stage's component check crashed, 'FortressLibrary.fss:988:7: I is not in the kind env [][]', and so did a generic trait's abstract method beside an object's, 'T is not in the kind env [][]'.
- The final (9697e3838) asks whether the implementing declaration's trait or object extends the abstract one's declaring trait at any depth. It reads the ancestors of the declaration with its static parameters in scope and compares the indexes by identity.

**Row 681, a size written with a static parameter in it.** `Formula.isNatTerm` let a size variable be bound only to a static parameter or a numeral (`Formula.scala:157` at the base), so `$i = i-1` had no solution. It now accepts an operation on static parameters and numerals, never one with a variable in it (`Formula.scala:156-162`). By the identity of sizes (`types-vals-vars.tex:55`), `IBox[\$i\]` and `IBox[\i-1\]` are one type once `$i` is `i-1`. So the call is applicable (`inference.tex:57`) and the argument fixes the parameter (`inference.tex:71`).

result.reportText:
# Rung A of climb batch 17: AnyList's comprises clause live, the rest of AnyList moved into List (row 636)

- problem: the distance's four sites of row 636, `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:12`, `:13`, `:14` and `:46` (`List.fss:89`, `:90`, `:88` and `:179` at the base)
- spec: `Specification/basic/traits.tex:235-245` (a listed type may hold a `where`-clause variable of the declaration, at every value of it)
- precedent: the size opening, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:853-885` at the base, and walk's symbolic type parameter, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/SingleFcn.java:170-171`, `:205-217`
- deviation: the probe's parent rule is scoped to a type `where`-clause variable; a parent that opens only sizes is opened as on the base, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:303-309`
- deviation: walk's comprises check at load reads a type `where`-clause variable as standing for any type, before the environment, beyond `processWhereClauses`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:1197-1198`, `:1463-1467`
- deviation: walk sets a type `where`-clause variable's bounds in a second pass, after every binding is in scope, as `SingleFcn.createSymbolicInstantiation` does, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:966-970`
- deviation: both calls of `openWhereSizes` pass the trait's static arguments, where the probe passed them in one of the two, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:852`, `:939-940`
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/disambiguator/TypeDisambiguator.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/staticenv/KindEnv.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`, `Library/List.fsi`, `Library/List.fss`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex` (all in the tree since `5a68404fd`, 2012-07-19)

## What changed and why

P-151 makes the team's comment on `AnyList` live (`Library/List.fsi:56`, `List.fss:87` at the base: "Not yet: comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]") and moves the rest of `AnyList` into `List`. The where-clause probe built the clause as a checker shadow (its REPORT, B.1). This rung takes B.1's lines only, re-based onto climb batch 16's `TypeAnalyzer`, and writes the library from the record.

- **The disambiguator** (`TypeDisambiguator.java:88-99`, `:111`, `:115-116`, `:120`, `:122`): a trait's type `where`-clause variables are in scope in its `where` clause, `comprises` clause, self type, parameters and members, not in its extends clause (`trait-parameters.tex`, "Where Clauses": a `where`-clause variable may not appear as a static argument in an extends clause). The phase is shared: on the base both paths refused the clause, "E is undefined."
- **The checker** (`TypeAnalyzer.scala`):
  - `whereSizes` (`:860-875`) returns a type binding too, as a type parameter with its binding's bounds;
  - `openWhereSizes` (`:901-915`) makes a fresh name `E#k` (`Formula.openedSizeName`, the counter the sizes use), bounded by its binding's bounds at the trait's static arguments. It registers the name in `KindEnv` and substitutes it. Both callers pass the arguments (`:852`, `:939-940`);
  - `opensTypes` (`:889-895`), new: a trait whose clause lists a type at a type `where`-clause variable;
  - the trait case of `pSubInner` (`:303-309`) does not open such a trait where it is reached as a parent of the type asked about. So `List[\E\]`, below `AnyList`, is not opened a second time to a fresh `List[\E#k\]`. A parent that opens only sizes is opened as on the base ("Decisions", 2).
  - The other code that opens reads `whereSizes`, and so takes types with no edit: the argument opening of a call (`impls/Functionals.scala:331-336`), the check of the extenders (`TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:319-323`, one inference variable per binding), `comprisedTypes` and `comprisesClause`.
- **The kind environment** (`KindEnv.scala:77-79`, `:142-155`): `EmptyKindEnv.lookup` finds an opened name in a registry at the end of `object KindEnv`, after `extractNodeBindings`, as the brief places it, apart from rung L's member after `makeFresh`. A name is registered once, with its bound, and never rebound.
- **Walk** (`BuildEnvironments.java`):
  - `processWhereClauses` (`:948-970`) binds a type `where`-clause variable as a `SymbolicInstantiatedType` with its bounds, as `SingleFcn.createSymbolicInstantiation` binds a type parameter, and sets the bounds in a second pass;
  - the comprises check at load (`ComprisesCheck`, `:1185`, `:1197-1198`, `:1463-1467`) reads such a variable as standing for any type. Without this, walk refused `object Box[\E\] extends AnyBox`: "Invalid comprises clause: AnyBox has a comprises clause but its immediate subtype Box is not eligible to extend it". The check reads the variable before the environment. A trait without static parameters has its component's environment as its interior (`BuildEnvironments.java:844`), so `processWhereClauses` binds the variable there, and the environment would answer with the symbolic type.
- **The library** (`List.fsi:56`, `List.fss:87-90`, `:173`):
  - the clause `comprises { List[\E\] } where [\E\]`;
  - `addLeft(e) = singleton(e) || self` and `addRight(e) = self || singleton(e)`, with the private `addL` and `addR` removed;
  - the list comprehension's unwrap: `cast[\CovariantCollection[\T\]\](cc).toImmutableArray()`.
  `AnyList`'s `||` stays `app(self, f)`, now accepted through the opened type. Part A's `appendAny` and `appendedTo` were not needed: the distance shows `app`'s site gone.
- **The specification** (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1438-1443`, `:1486-1508`, `:1537-1540`): the Effect of "The traits that extend a closed trait" says what the checker and the interpreter now do, with the departures as rows. Its Rationale names the decision, and its last item says what undoing it needs.

## The test first, then the fix

The failing runs ended before the edit was first built (`ant compileAll` started at 14:35:01 UTC).

    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests OpenTypeChecker.test XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker.test XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker.test XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker.test

    2) ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker(...)AssertionFailedError: Saw wrong failure. compile
    4) ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker(...)AssertionFailedError: Saw wrong failure. compile

    (14:29:07 UTC, on the base's code and library)
    tmp/rung-anylist-comprises/h1/tests/OpenTypeWalk.fss:5:31:
        E is undefined.
    Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0

The brief expected walk to stop at load with "Missing type E". That was the probe's run, with its disambiguator change in. On the base, the shared disambiguator refuses first.

`AnyListElementTypeWalk` guards the element types that `AnyList`'s bodies give under walk, the probe's A.2.2 cases. It passed on the base library before the library edit (14:30:35 UTC, `OK (1 test)`).

`NatOpenThroughSubtraitChecker` is the test of the second fix, the parent rule scoped to types. It passes on the old code, and it failed on `b6cb13000`, the first change, before `c6adc85f1` was built:

    explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base17 <tree>/tmp/old-caches junit <tree>/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NatOpenThroughSubtraitChecker.test

    Tests run: 2,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0

The passing runs are on the final code: `c6adc85f1`, built at 14:58. `fa7f66b44` adds a test and text, in the same code state.

## Suites, once on the final code state

The edit changes the checker (Scala), walk (Java) and a shared phase, the disambiguator. So both suites ran, and `ant testSpecData` ran because walk loads the new clause (P-124). All three ran on `c6adc85f1`'s code.

## The checker's count and time (P-148)

Each run is `time explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh $W/tmp/rung-anylist-comprises/count/$N.txt $W/tmp/rung-anylist-comprises/count/$N`, all in one session, on a machine shared with rung C (load 6 to 10).

- **The tables**: `diff explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-16/gate/checker-count.txt` against the change's table prints nothing (`#total 39`, `#locations 38`, `#crash none`). The base run's table equals the gate's too.

- **The time**: the difference in real time comes from the load; the user time is the same. Not a finding.
- **The profile**: JFR, `settings=profile`, of the count's driver on the final code, 6,744 samples.
  - Its top frames are the base's: `Walker.walkCases7$` 5.25 %, `ASTGenHelper$.scalaify` 4.34 %, `Walker.walkCases0` 3.97 %, `Statics.anyHash` 3.93 %, `Walker.walkCases2` 3.50 %, `BoxesRunTime.equals2` 3.48 %.

- **The memo keys**: no memo was added. An opened name is fresh at each opening, and is registered once with its bound. So a key that holds `E#k` holds every input that an answer about it reads.
  - The subtype memo and the ground memo skip a question whose left type opens (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:114`, now true of a type opening too).
  - The trait case no longer opens a type-opening parent, so no fresh type arises inside a memoized question on that path.
  - The exclusion memo and the reduction memo keep no answer whose computation opened (`:426-428`, `:605-607`; the counter is shared with the sizes).

# Rung A of climb batch 17: the record lines

## FACTS

- **A type `where`-clause variable of a `comprises` clause is opened at a call, as a size is, and `AnyList`'s clause is live.**
  - The compiled checker gives an argument whose trait lists `Box[\E\] where [\E\]` a fresh type of its own for the call, bounded as the binding is.
  - It refuses that type where another type is declared, gives two values two types, and refuses Amin and Tate's shape. It does not open such a trait where it reaches it as a parent.
  - Walk binds the variable as a symbolic type at load.
  - With `AnyList`'s `addLeft`, `addRight` and the comprehension's unwrap respelled, the distance goes from 49 to 45 (row 636's four sites). The count, and walk's element types, are unchanged.
  - Tests: `OpenTypeChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker`, `OpenTypeWalk`, `AnyListElementTypeWalk`.
  - Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-anylist-comprises/REPORT.md`.

## Ledger notes

- Row 636: close it. Commits `b6cb13000` and `c6adc85f1`, test `OpenTypeChecker`. Note: "climb batch 17 rung A: the clause made live (opened at a call by the checker, bound at load by walk), with `AnyList`'s `addLeft`, `addRight` and the comprehension's unwrap respelled; the distance's `List.fss:88`, `:89`, `:90` and `:179` are gone (49 to 45); walk's element types are unchanged (`AnyListElementTypeWalk`)."
- Row 682: append "climb batch 17 rung A: the opening covers a type where-clause variable too, and the type face is refused the same way: `f(x: AnyBox)` beside `f[\E\](x: Box[\E\])`, for `trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E\]`, 'There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type: AnyBox' (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOpenTypeOverloadChecker.test`); walk runs the generic one."
- Row 701: append "climb batch 17 rung A: a trait with a type where-clause variable stops the code generator the same way, 'Can't compile TraitDecl AnyBox' (`XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker`'s program made well typed), so the type opening's tests are typecheck tests or refusals."
- Row 307: append "climb batch 17 rung A: the checker opens a type where-clause variable of a comprises clause as it opens a size; the code generator reads neither off an argument, behind row 701."

## New rows (section "2. Types: generics, static parameters, inference and coercion")

| NEW-A-1 | the compiled checker opens a trait whose `comprises` clause lists a type at a `where`-clause variable also as a function type's result, once for all results: it accepts `apply2(g)`, `apply2[\nat n\](f: ZZ32 -> Nt[\n\]): ZZ32 = two(f(1), f(2))`, for a `g(i: ZZ32): NatParamT` of two sizes | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (checker) | `basic/trait-parameters.tex`, "Nat and Int Parameters" | none | climb batch 17 rung A | Sizes on the base (3aea3da53), types since rung A: the same program over `trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E\]` is accepted. `bin/fortress typecheck` prints no error for either; walk stops at the call, 'Cannot unify ZZ32->NatParamT ... with ZZ32->Nt[\n\]'. The opening is the trait case of `pSubInner` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala`), reached through the arrow case's range. The specification opens an argument whose own type is such a trait. No gated test shows it: a compiled refusal test is red while the program is accepted. |

| NEW-A-2 | the compiled checker does not open, as a parent, a trait whose `comprises` clause lists a type at a type `where`-clause variable: a value of an unlisted trait below it, `Mid[\ZZ32\]` for `trait Mid[\E\] extends AnyBox` and `object Box[\E\] extends Mid[\E\]`, is refused where `Box[\F\]` is expected | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | design limit (checker) | silent | `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOpenTypeThroughSubtraitChecker.test` | climb batch 17 rung A | 'is not applicable to an argument of type Mid[\ZZ32\]'. Not opening such a parent keeps a listed type from a second opening, `List[\E\]` through `AnyList`, which cost List 22 sites in the where-clause probe. A parent that lists a type at a size is opened as on the base, so the same shape at a size is accepted (`NatOpenThroughSubtraitChecker`). Walk runs the program. In the library only `List` extends `AnyList`. |

Both rows pass `ledger.py check --rows` with a number in place of the placeholder. `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1497` and `:1502` cite them as `NEW-A-2` and `NEW-A-1`.

## Handover

Climb batch 17's rung A (`wip/rung-anylist-comprises`, `fa7f66b44`) did the following:
- `AnyList`'s clause is live: the checker opens a type `where`-clause variable at a call as it opens a size, and walk binds it at load.
- The distance goes from 49 to 45 (row 636's four sites); the count stays at 39.
- Rows NEW-A-1 (the opening under a function type's result, sizes and types) and NEW-A-2 (a type-opening parent is not opened) are open, and row 682 has a type face.

## Revival change

**The change.**
- The team's source: the team's library carried the clause as a comment on `AnyList`, "Not yet: comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]" (`Library/List.fsi:56`, `List.fss:87` before this change), and wrote `AnyList`'s `addLeft` and `addRight` through the private `addL` and `addR` (`List.fss:89-90`, `:102-106` before).
- What both paths did: the disambiguator, which both paths share, refused a type `where`-clause variable in a `comprises` clause, "E is undefined." The compiled checker refused four of `AnyList`'s and the comprehension's calls, reading their arguments as a list of an unknown element type. For example: "Could not check call to function app ... is not applicable to an argument of type (List.AnyList, List.AnyList)" at `List.fss:88`, and "No such method CovariantCollection.AnyCovColl.toImmutableArray" at `:179`.
- What the tree now does:
  - The clause is live (`List.fsi:56`, `List.fss:87`).
  - A trait's type `where`-clause variables are in scope in the trait but for its extends clause.
  - The checker opens such a variable at a call, as it opens a size: the argument takes the listed type at a type of its own, bounded as the binding is, and known to equal only itself (`OpenTypeChecker`). The checker refuses that type where another is declared, and gives two values two types (`XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker`). It does not open such a trait where it reaches it as a parent (`XXXOpenTypeThroughSubtraitChecker`).
  - Walk binds the variable as a type that stands for every type when it loads the trait, and its check at load reads a listed type at every type (`OpenTypeWalk`).
  - `addLeft` and `addRight` are `singleton(e) || self` and `self || singleton(e)`, and the comprehension's unwrap casts its collection to `CovariantCollection[\T\]`. Walk's element types are unchanged (`AnyListElementTypeWalk`).
- The reason:
  - the team's comment;
  - `Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations", which lets a listed type hold a `where`-clause variable of the declaration at every value of it;
  - the checker's four refusals above.
- The departures: the opening also under a function type's result (row NEW-A-1); an unlisted extender is not opened (row NEW-A-2); the code generator does not compile a trait with a `where` clause (row 701).

**Provenance.**
- The decision: P-151, the curator's decision of 16 October 2026, "the team's comment `AnyList comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]` becomes live ... the rest of `AnyList` moves into `List`", built from the where-clause probe's B.1 and A.2.2.
- The batch: climb batch 17, rung A.
- The scope of the parent rule to type openings is this rung's decision, on the evidence of `NatOpenThroughSubtraitChecker`, and is listed for review.

# Rung G of climb batch 17: walk's load check reads every pair of generic declarations by the checker's rules

- problem: walk refused two generic functions unless a parameter pair excluded (row 159, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:299`), and loaded two declarations whose declared domains are equal (rows 742 and 549, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:351`, `:340`); the five tests of section 2 were red on the base through the harness.
- spec: `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-110` (a declaration with static parameters is read over its instances and compared on the parameter types it declares; the rules are in `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:531-575`, "Declarations with Static Parameters").
- precedent: `genericPairValid`, climb batch 16's reading of a withdrawn pair on its declared domains (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:842`, at the base `:801`), and the generic-beside-plain branch of `validOnDeclaredDomains`, which refuses `plainInside && genInside` (at the base `:781-783`).
- deviation: the refusal of equal declared domains reads a pair that the parameter check passed, which no precedent reads, and gives the team's message for equal parameter lists (`OverloadedFunction.java:628`, the team's `:573` at `a874948ac`) for two lists that differ as written (`OverloadedFunction.java:533-540`).
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java`, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex` (each a file of the 2012 tree; every line changed in them is the revival's).

## 1. What changed and why

P-45 decides that walk's load check reads every pair of generic declarations on their declared domains by the checker's rules, with no parameter pair required to exclude (row 159). Climb batch 16 built that reading only for a pair some parameter pair of which had excluded in walk's reading of each at a symbolic instantiation and then had the exclusion withdrawn (F-238). This rung widens it to every pair, and adds the No Duplicates Rule for the pairs that the parameter check orders wrongly (rows 742 and 549).

In `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java` (commit `b5a497c04`):

- `validOnDeclaredDomains` (`:750-793`) reads a pair of two own generics that the parameter check refuses by `genericPairValid` whether or not an exclusion was withdrawn: `return genericPairValid(o1, o2, all);` (`:766`) in place of `return withdrawn && genericPairValid(o1, o2, all);`. `genericPairValid` (`:842`) is unchanged: refused where each declared domain lies inside the other (No Duplicates), valid where one lies inside the other and its return type is below at the holding instance (Return Type), else valid where a third declaration below both holds the overlap (`genericMeetCovered`, Meet).
- `completeOverloadingCheck` (`:528-540`): a pair that the check passes without an excluding parameter is read again by `sameDeclaredDomains` (`:795-822`, with `declaredInside`, `:824-832`): where one at least is an own generic and the other an own generic or a declaration without static parameters, and each declared domain lies inside the other (each generic's over its own instances, by `instanceHolding`), the pair is refused, "Overloading of ... and ... fails because their parameter lists have the same types". The parameter check reads a type parameter `T` as strictly below its bound `Wide` and sets `p1better`, so it orders `tie[\T extends Wide\](a: T, b: T)` before `tie(a: Wide, b: Wide)` or `tie[\T extends Wide\](a: Wide, b: Wide)`, though at the bound the two declared domains are one.
- The `withdrawn` field, its reset and its one assignment go, since nothing reads it now (at the base `:310-312`, `:340`, `:479`).
- The two comments that climb batch 16's judge left (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-16/JUDGE-review.md:136-138`) read F-238's reading: the loop's comment (`:464-466`), "Read each at a symbolic instantiation of its static parameters, shared where both declare the same ones", and `validOnDeclaredDomains`'s comment (`:757-761`), which now says that every refused pair of two own generics is read on its declared domains. The field's comment (at the base `:310-311`) went with the field.

The object-type shortcut (`:437-443`, `:509`, row 697's) and rung W's `bestMatchWithCoercion` and `bestMatchInternal` are untouched; a three-way merge with `origin/wip/rung-walk-method-sargs` is clean (`git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/wip/rung-walk-method-sargs` exits 0).

The specification's two revival sentences on these rows are edited (section 4).

| `XXXDispatchRenamedArmWalkRungG` (row 159) | `DispatchRenamedGenericArmWalk` | none (loads and dispatches) |
